metadata.note: The Columbia, Newberry and Laurens Railroad (chartered 1885 as the Newberry and Laurens, renamed 24 Dec 1886; reporting mark CNL) ran from Columbia through Irmo, Chapin, Little Mountain, Prosperity and Newberry to Dover Junction just short of Clinton (completed July 1891), and from 1896 on to Laurens over the former Laurens Railway. Drawn: the South Carolina Railway's lessee operation Columbia - Clinton 1891-1892; the CN&L's own trains Columbia - Clinton 1892-1952 and Clinton - Laurens 1896-1952. The 1891-1892 lessee era is a Rule 4 split on identical geometry. ACL stock control (1924/1926) did not change who ran the trains and is not split. Passenger service ended 1952 (secondary sources); the line stayed in freight service as the CN&L until the 1984 merger into CSX and is today the CSX CN&L Subdivision (not drawn, Rule 1).

metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) PASSENGER END 1952: secondary only (carolana, Wikipedia, american-rails - probably all from F. Will Martin's 2013 book); no primary source dates the end, the month is unknown, and the Feb 1952 Official Guide's CN&L table is present but its times are unreadable. A Dec 1954 Guide (cited by Wikipedia) or a 1951-53 newspaper discontinuance notice would settle it. (2) 1890 OPERATOR: passenger trains ran Columbia - Prosperity by July 1890 and to Newberry by Oct 1890, but the South Carolina Railway lease is only confirmed from the Aug 1891 timetable; 1890 is therefore not drawn under any company. (3) SAL OPERATION 1893-c.1895: the July 1893 annual meeting says the Seaboard Air Line 'will operate' the CN&L the ensuing year, and W. G. Childs was both CN&L president and SAL's Columbia representative in Dec 1894, but no SAL-headed CN&L timetable was found; drawn as CN&L. If a 1893-1895 schedule shows SAL operating, split a SAL feature. (4) ACL 'lease' Jun 1892 - Jul 1893 treated as no split (CN&L-headed timetable, CN&L officers) - a judgement call. (5) Headways and speeds are estimates beyond the 1891 and 1896 timetables. (6) ACL control date 1924 vs 1926 and Laurens Railway sale 1894 vs 1895/96 - conflicts recorded in segment notes. (7) Exact site of Dover Junction and of the CN&L's own pre-1996 alignment into Clinton (geometry_quality). (8) Location of the pre-1902 Columbia Union Depot.

properties.geometry_quality: Columbia - Clinton: traced 66.8 mi against a documented 65.5 mi (Fowler / 1915 Rand McNally mileposts, Columbia Union Depot 0.0 - Clinton 65.5; 63.5 mi Columbia - Dover Junction per carolana/american-rails) - 1.9% long. No straight-line (approximated) legs. Mileage by OSM operator tag (opstrace report plus the two hand-routed terminal approaches): CN&L-tagged 60.9 mi, untagged rail 2.2 mi (mostly through Newberry, incl. the abandoned 'Old CN&L Main'), SAL-tagged 3.4 mi (see below), Southern-tagged 0.1 mi, 0.05 mi of graph connector. Traced chainage vs Fowler: Gervais St 1.4/1.6, Irmo 12.1/10.6, Ballentine 16.6/15.3, White Rock 19.3/18.1, Chapin 24.5/23.0, Little Mountain 29.7/28.5, Prosperity 37.3/35.9, Newberry 44.4/43.1, Kinard 57.7/56.1, Joanna (Goldville) 60.9/59.6, Clinton 66.8/65.5 - a fairly constant +1.2-1.5 mi that appears between Columbia and Irmo and was not explained (possibly a realignment there, or Fowler's atlas-derived mileposts). Every waypoint lies within 0.4 km of the line. ERA / ALIGNMENT CAVEATS: (1) drawn on the alignment OSM maps today (the live CSX freight line); 1891-1952 line changes were not checked. (2) COLUMBIA TERMINAL: from the CN&L's junction at Elmwood the last ~2 mi into Union Station are drawn over the CSX Columbia Sub (old_railway_operator SAL, 1.35 mi) and untagged/NS station trackage (0.6 mi); the CN&L's actual trackage route into Union Depot was not established, and the drawn end is the 1902 Union Station building - the location of the pre-1902 Union Depot was not checked. (3) CLINTON: OSM has no trace of the CN&L's own pre-1996 alignment through Dover Junction into Clinton (none in OSM abandoned/historic tags or OHM). From the point where the CN&L-tagged way 188358711 joins the CSX Monroe Sub (-81.8488, 34.4599) the last 2.1 mi into Clinton are drawn on Monroe Sub track tagged old_railway_operator SAL. That track continues the CN&L's own curve straight on and is probably the historic CN&L (or within a few hundred metres of it), but this is unverified; the 1996 CSX connector is not knowingly drawn, and the eastern Monroe Sub loop is not used. Dover Junction - Clinton (about 2 mi) was Laurens Railway track used by CN&L trains 1891-1895, the CN&L's own from 1896.

segments.note: CN&L operating its own trains from 'Time Table No. 1, to take effect Sunday, June 5th' [1892], signed J. R. Kenly, General Manager (an ACL officer) and W. G. Childs, Superintendent (Lexington Dispatch 13 Sep 1893). The July 1893 annual meeting said the road had been 'leased and operated by the Atlantic Coast Line for the past year' and that the Seaboard Air Line 'will operate' it the ensuing year (Columbia Register 19 Jul 1893, reprinted Newberry H&N 26 Jul 1893); the public timetable stayed the CN&L's own, so no ACL split is drawn and a SAL operation 1893-c.1895 is UNPROVEN (agreement found, no SAL-headed timetable) - see metadata.not_yet_sourced. Trains ran Columbia - Dover Junction - Clinton over the Laurens Railway's track for the last ~2 mi. Segment ends where the April 1896 through Columbia - Laurens timetable begins (era boundary, not a gap). Headway is an ESTIMATE (about one round trip a day); the report records no train count for 1892-1896. Trains used Columbia Union Station (drawn terminal) until the early 1930s, then the CN&L's own station at 630 Gervais Street (about MP 1.4-1.6 on the drawn line). Steam-hauled to the end (carolana).

segments.note: CN&L's own through Columbia - Clinton - Laurens timetable in effect 30 Apr 1896 ('The Short Line to Greenville, Spartanburg and Glenn Springs', W. G. Childs Superintendent; passenger Nos. 52/53 plus local freight Nos. 1/2 whose passenger-carrying status is not stated; Lexington Dispatch 15 Jul 1896). Headway 720 is an ESTIMATE from that one daily passenger train each way; american-rails mentions 'four CN&L passenger trains a day' at Clinton at an unstated date, and an ACL Charleston - Greenville through train used the CN&L from about 1910 (american-rails; who crewed it is unresolved, not drawn separately). The Atlantic Coast Line bought control of the CN&L's stock (1924 per Wikipedia/carolana; ICC authorisation 4 Nov 1926 per american-rails - conflict recorded), but the CN&L remained a separate corporation running its own trains under its own name and officers (the 1952 Guide prints its own heading, president T. P. Taylor of Columbia, ACL president C. McD. Davis as chairman), so this is not a Rule 4 ownership split. Trains used Columbia Union Station (drawn terminal) until the early 1930s, then the CN&L's own station at 630 Gervais Street (about MP 1.4-1.6 on the drawn line). Steam-hauled to the end (carolana). PASSENGER END 1952 IS SECONDARY-SOURCED: 'service was discontinued in 1952' comes from carolana.com, Wikipedia and american-rails.com, which probably share one origin (F. Will Martin's 2013 book, 'The Columbia, Newberry, and Laurens Railroad: The Dutch Fork Line'); no primary source for the end was found and the month is unknown. The Feb 1952 Official Guide still prints a CN&L entry with its own officers and a table (Prosperity 35.9, Newberry 43.1, Joanna, one stray '4 00 PM'), but its time columns are too damaged by OCR to prove a train. Freight continued after 1952 (CN&L until the 1984 merger into CSX, today the CSX CN&L Subdivision) - not drawn (Rule 1).

END YEAR 1952 rests only on secondary sources (carolana, Wikipedia, american-rails - likely one origin) plus the presence of a CN&L table in the Feb 1952 Official Guide; no primary source dates the end. Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Ex-Laurens Railway line, sold to the CN&L at foreclosure (sale 30 Dec 1895, conveyed 15 Jan 1896 per the ICC valuation corporate table; Wikipedia's Laurens Railway article says 1894 - conflict recorded, not used). The CN&L's through Columbia - Clinton - Laurens timetable was in effect 30 Apr 1896 (No. 53 lv Laurens 1:45 pm; Lexington Dispatch 15 Jul 1896). A Newberry Observer column's 'daily Columbia - Laurens trains beginning in 1902' conflicts with that timetable; the timetable is preferred. This line's years before 1896 belong to the Laurens Railroad/Railway (Richmond & Danville-controlled from 1888), not the CN&L, and are not drawn here. Connection at Laurens with the Charleston & Western Carolina (shared Laurens Union depot). Headway 720 is an ESTIMATE from one daily passenger train each way in 1896. The Atlantic Coast Line bought control of the CN&L's stock (1924 per Wikipedia/carolana; ICC authorisation 4 Nov 1926 per american-rails - conflict recorded), but the CN&L remained a separate corporation running its own trains under its own name and officers (the 1952 Guide prints its own heading, president T. P. Taylor of Columbia, ACL president C. McD. Davis as chairman), so this is not a Rule 4 ownership split. The Feb 1952 Official Guide still prints a CN&L entry with its own officers and a table (Prosperity 35.9, Newberry 43.1, Joanna, one stray '4 00 PM'), but its time columns are too damaged by OCR to prove a train. Freight continued after 1952 (CN&L until the 1984 merger into CSX, today the CSX CN&L Subdivision) - not drawn (Rule 1).
